The high-return language is presented as quoted or reported discussion of an investor and fund strategy, without a guaranteed viewer outcome or required payment. The separately promoted 21Shares service is identified as paid sponsorship with risk and jurisdictional qualifications.

opening.argument: Judge, the crypto discussion does not end at reporting what institutions hold. The speaker names Bitcoin and crypto as an investment theme, then directs interested viewers to 21Shares; the description supplies a link to that company. rebuttal.rebuttal: The portfolio filings explain part of the video, but they do not account for the transition from the Bitcoin theme to a named crypto-product provider and a link to it. Sponsorship disclosure establishes who paid for that transition; it does not make the resulting invitation merely neutral analysis. Nor does the absence of a guaranteed return erase the invitation to explore an investment product.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the combined impression. A headline says big money is buying heavily; the speaker highlights Harvard's Bitcoin ETF holding and says major institutions are moving into Bitcoin and crypto. The video also raises the prospect that investors pursuing greater growth might see 5X, 10X, or perhaps 100X, while its description sends viewers to a crypto-product provider. The multiple-return remark concerns AI infrastructure, not 21Shares products. Still, placing extraordinary upside language in the same investment presentation as institutional crypto buying and an external product link makes the promotion more concerning than an isolated market update.
